## 1. A drug on a filament

1. Open [PDB 1JFF](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/1JFF). Read its title and experimental method.
2. Choose **3D View** to open Mol*. Find **TA1 (taxol)** in the small-molecule/ligand list.
   Select it, zoom to its surroundings, and identify the contacting tubulin chain.
3. Read the polymer descriptions to distinguish α- and β-tubulin. Save the PDB ID,
   ligand code and method in your report. A structure is one state, not a movie.

## 2. Drugs can change the same motor in opposite directions

1. Open [PDB 5N69](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/5N69). Identify the motor and ligand.
2. Read the title carefully: this is **omecamtiv mecarbil**, a cardiac myosin activator.
3. Open the [EXPLORER-HCM record, NCT03470545](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03470545).
   Read **Conditions**, **Interventions**, **Study type**, **Phase** and **Outcome measures**.
   Mavacamten is a cardiac myosin inhibitor. Do not label 5N69 a mavacamten structure.
4. Search RCSB for `mavacamten`, open a matching experimental entry, and record its
   accession and species. Distinguish a solved structure from an AlphaFold model.

## 3. Variants and tissues

1. Open human [KRT14, P02533](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P02533/entry)
   and [MYH7, P12883](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P12883/entry).
2. Follow their **Pathology & Biotech** disease links to ClinVar. Choose one
   pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant per gene. Record its HGVS expression,
   ClinVar accession, condition, review status and date. Record conflicting submissions if present.
3. Read the GTEx gene pages for [KRT14](https://gtexportal.org/home/gene/KRT14)
   and [MYH7](https://gtexportal.org/home/gene/MYH7). Is each distribution plausible
   for an epithelial filament protein or cardiac motor?

## Tasks

**T1.** Which tubulin subunit binds taxol in 1JFF? How does stabilising microtubules affect mitosis? `[ELO 6, 9]`

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer (checked 2026-11-18)"}
Taxol binds **β-tubulin**. Suppressing microtubule dynamics impairs spindle rearrangement and chromosome segregation; it does not simply dissolve the microtubules. The structure uses electron crystallography of zinc-induced sheets, not an intact spindle.
:::

**T2.** Why might inhibition of myosin help in one heart disease while activation is explored in another? `[ELO 6, 9]`

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer (checked 2026-11-18)"}
A hypercontractile motor can contribute to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, whereas insufficient force is a different problem. A shared target does not imply the same desired direction of change. A trial registration describes the tested hypothesis; registration alone does not establish benefit.
:::

**T3.** What diseases connect to KRT14 and MYH7? Does every variant in either gene cause the same disease? `[ELO 9]`

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer (checked 2026-11-18)"}
KRT14 defects can cause **epidermolysis bullosa simplex**, where fragile epithelial cells fail under stress. MYH7 variants can cause **hypertrophic cardiomyopathy** and other cardiac or skeletal myopathies. Variant-specific evidence and the named phenotype matter; a gene name alone is not a diagnosis.
:::
